answer: Binding each account to one device key turns fakery into a hardware problem. A new agent registers its key on one device, which may carry only one active identity; moving it to a fresh account starts a 30-day cooldown freezing accrued credit. A hollow shell account is not free: 100 fakes need 100 devices, and each switch costs a month of earnings. Peers check the signature per job, so a mismatch stands out like a plume of smoke, and both accounts freeze for review. Newcomers still join one device at a time, like a lotus opening, since the rule caps parallel fakery.
